Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Call to Order/Roll Call With Invocation & Pledge
CALL TO ORDER:  Maria Davila, Mayor

INVOCATION:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources

ROLL CALL:  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

Presentations
  1. City's Budget and Fiscal Future

  The City Council will consider receiving and filing a presentation on the City's Budget and
  Fiscal Future. (AS)

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall

  2
 be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items
Agenda Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including Ordinances,
Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent Calendar,
individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion of these
items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific items be
removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members of the
public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three (3)
minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk

  6
 Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

  SUBJECT: ORDINANCE  REDUCING  CITIZENS'  Al)VISORY  COMMITTEE  FROM  20
  TO 10 APPOINTED  MEMBERS

  PURPOSE:  To introduce an Ordinance amending the number of appointments to the Citizens'
  Advisory Committee ("CAC") from 20 members to 10 members appointed by the City Council.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider introducing  an Ordinance
  amending Section 1.25.020 (Membership) of Chapter 1.25 (Citizens' Advisory Committee),  of
  Title 1 (Administration  and Personnel), of the South Gate Municipal Code to reduce the number
  of appointed comi'nittee members to ten (10) entitling each Council Member to appoint two (2)
  committee members from among qualified residents of the city who are eighteen years of age or
  older. Before taking office, each committee member shall be confirmed by a majority vote of the
  City  Council.

  FISCAL IMPACT:  CAC members receive a stipend of $25 per meeting.  The reduction  of
  members from 20 to 10 will yield a savings of $250 per meeting.

  ANALYSIS:  The City Council is being asked to provide direction as to whether an ordinance
  should be presented for consideration to change the membership number of the advisory body.

  Should the City Council approve the introduction and adopt the Ordinance, it would be effective
  in December 2025. At that time, City Council Members would be asked to submit their nominees
  to be agendize for City Council approval. The goal would be to convene the first meeting of the
  new Commission in time to consider the Coinmunity Development Block Grant ("CDBG") awards
  for FY2026-27.

  BACKGROUND:  The CAC is an advisory coininittee to the City Council. The City Council, by
  state law, is the responsible legislative body in matters relating to the annual action plan process.
  The CAC is involved in the development of the annual action plan and the development and/or
  review of all elements pertaining to the planning and preparation of the CDBG Program. The
  committee assesses community development needs and reviews comi'nunity  objectives whenever
  deemed necessary and provides recomi'nendations on the use of CDBG funds to the City Council.

  1

 The  CAC  currently  meets  on an as-needed  basis  (meeting  up to six  (6) times  a year)  and is
comprised  of 20 members  appointed  by the City  Council.  In recent  years,  filling  all committee
seats has proven  challenging,  and achieving  a quorum  formeetings  has also been an ongoing  issue.
Staff  recoinmend  reducing  the  number  of  CAC  members  to improve  the  manageability  of
appointments  and to increase  the likelihood  of reaching  a quorum  for future  meetings.

 CONSTRUCTION  OF THE  SEWER  LINING  PROJECT,  CITY  PROJECT  N0.  709-SW

PURPOSE:  The City  manages  an extensive  sewer collection  system  consisting  of pipelines,
manholes,  and service laterals, much of which  requires  ongoing  rehabilitation  to extend its usefiil
life. Project  construction  was completed  under budget.  Contract  Change Order No. 8 authorizes
additional improvements  to the City's  sewer system. These improvements  will  address existing
deficiencies, enhance system reliability,  and utilize available ARPA funding.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Contract  Change  Order  No. 8 to Contract  No. 2024-100-CC  ("Agreement")
  with  Vortex  Services,  LLC,  dba Sancon  Technologies,  to rehabilitate  24 manholes  at
  various locations under the Sewer  Lining  Project,  City  Project  No.  709-SW,  in the
  amount of $133,800; and
  b.  Authorizing the Assistant  City  Manager/Director  of Public  Works  to execute  Contract
  Change Order No. 8.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no impact  to the General Fund. CCO No. 8 to the Agreement  is in
the amount  of $133,800  and will  be funded with American  Rescue Plan Act (ARPA)  Funds. The
total Project budget is $3,000,000  which  is planned  to be expended  as summarized  below.

ANALYSIS:  The City  received  $3 million  in ARPA  funds  to rehabilitate  sewer  pipelines  and
manholes  throughout  the  City's  sewer  system.  Construction  of  the  original  project  was
completed  $138,229.58  under  budget,  leaving  those funds  available  for additional  improvements.

With  City  Council  support,  Change  Order  No.  8 in the amount  of $133,800  will  fund  epoxy
lining  and rehabilitation  of approximately  24 manholes  located  within  the original  project  area.
The project  is fully  funded  with  ARPA  funds,  which  carry  strict  federal  deadlines  and eligibility
criteria.  These funds  must be spent within  the approved  contract  scope, and any unspent  balance
cannot  be reprogrammed  once the funding  deadline  has passed.

The  additional  work  is scheduled  to begin  in early  November  and be completed  by December
2025, with 20 additional  working  days allocated  to finish  the improvements.  Change  Order  No. 8
is priced  consistent  with  the bid rates for manhole  rehabilitation  in the original  contract.

BACKGROUND:  The City  of South  Gate's  Public  Works  Department  maintains  approximately
120 miles  of sewer  pipelines  that  carry  wastewater  from  homes  and businesses  to the regional
treatment  system  operated  by the Los  Angeles  County  Sanitation  Districts.  The network  also
includes  about  2,400  manholes  and 19,500  service  connections  (laterals)  that  link  individual
properties  to the City's  main  sewer  lines.  Most  of the system  is made of concrete  and clay pipes,
ranging  in size from  4 to 27 inches  in diameter.

On December  10, 2024,  the City  Council  awarded  the Sewer  Lining  Project  contract  to Sancon
Technologies,  Inc. in the amount  of $2,143,727.  At the same meeting,  the City  Council  approved
Change  Order  No. 1, which  reduced  the total  contract  amount  by $526,745,  resulting  in a revised
contract  total  of $1,616,982.  Subsequent  to the contract  award,  Sancon  Technologies,  Inc.  was
acquired  by Vortex  Services,  LLC,  which  completed  the project  under  the same contract.

Construction  began  in March  2025  and reached  substantial  completion  on September  26, 2025,
inclusive  of  all  approved  change  order  work.  During  construction,  it  was  necessary  to
administratively  approve  Change  Orders  Nos.  2 through  7, totaling  $181,362.87,  to address
unforeseen  field  conditions  encountered  during  the project.  All  change  orders  were  approved
within  the  City  Manager's  $250,000  administrative  authority  granted  at the time  of contract
award.  These  adjustments  ensured  the project  remained  on schedule  and allowed  for additional
sewer system  improvements  to be completed  without  delay.

SUBJECT:  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES AGREEMENT  WITH SA ASSOCIATES,  INC.
TO PREPARE DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION  DOCUMENTS  FOR THE FIRESTONE
BOULEVARD  PIPELINE  REPLACEMENT  PROJECT, CITY PROJECT N0. 737-WTR

PURPOSE:  To award an Agreement to SA Associates, Inc., ("SA") to prepare  design and
construction  documents necessary for the Firestone Boulevard Pipeline Replacement  Project.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will  consider:
  a.  Approving  a Professional Services Agreement  with SA to prepare design and
  construction documents for the Firestone Boulevard Pipeline Replacement Project, City
  ProjectNo. 737-WIR, for an amount not to exceed $356,000;
  b.  Appropriating  $100,000 in Water Funds to fiilly fund the budget for the Firestone
  Boulevard Pipeline Replacement Project, City ProjectNo. 737-WTR;
  c.  Authorizing the City Manager to approve and execute amendments up to a cumulative
  amount of $100,000; and
  d.  Authorizing the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable to the City
  Attorney.

FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no impact to the General Fund. The Agreement is in the amount of
$356,000 and it will be fully funded with Water Funds. The project budget proposed is $407,000
in Water Funds, of which $307,000 is currently budgeted and $100,000 is a recommended
appropriation. Planned budget services are summarized  below.

  Design Phase Services  Water  Funds
  Professional  Services  Agreement  $356,000
  Contingency  $36,00
  City  Staff  Time  $15,000
  Total Budget  $407,000

ANALYSIS:  The City issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) on PlanetBids for engineering services
needed for the Firestone Boulevard Pipeline Replacement Project. Proposals were received from MNS
and SA Associates on March 14, 2025. Following evaluation by the designated selection committee,
MNS was initially ranked as the highest qualified consultant and selected for negotiations. However,
negotiations with MNS were unsuccessful. As such, the City proceeded to negotiate with the second

  1  117
   highest ranked qualified  consultant,  SA Associates,  and successfully  reached an agreement.  The selection
  committee  deemed SA Associates  qualifiedto  performthe  work, m'idthey  aretherefore  recommended  for
  the contract. Their proposed  service fees of $356,000  are reasonable and within  the industty  standard for
  this type of service.

  BACKGROUND:  The City  operates  a municipal  water  system  with  approximately  135 miles
  of water  mains,  serving  more  than 14,250  residential,  commercial,  and industrial  customers.  The
  water  pipeline  located  on the  Firestone  Boulevard  Bridge  over  the  Los  Angeles  River  has
  deteriorated  and requires  replacement.  This  project  will  replace  that pipeline  and also remove
  and replace  the section  of pipeline  that crosses the I-710  Freeway.

  The Public  Works  Department  is recommending  awarding  a Professional  Services  Agreement  to
  SA  to  prepare  design  and  construction  documents  for  the  Firestone  Boulevard  Pipeline
  Replacement  Project.  SA  was  selected  through  a competitive  Request  for  Proposals  ("RFP")
  process.  On April  9, 2025,  an RFP  for engineering  services  was released.  Two  proposals  were
  submitted  to the City  Clerk's  Office  by MNS  in the amount  of $800,000  and SA Associates  in
  the amount  of $356,000.

  A  selection  committee  was  formed  consisting  of  the  Water  Resources  Manager,  Associate
  Engineer  and Water  Manager.  The committee  evaluated  the proposal  and interviewed  MNS  and
  SA Associates.  Upon  completion  of the evaluation  process,  MNS  was identified  as the highest
ranked  consultant  and invited  to negotiate  a contract.  Negotiations,  however,  did not result  in an
agreement.  Accordingly,  the  City  commenced  negotiations  with  the  second  highest  ranked
  qualified  consultant,  SA Associates,  and successfully  finalized  terms.  SA Associates  has been
determined  to be qualified  to perform  the required  services  and is recommended  for  contract
award.

SA Associates  offers  the following:

*  Qualified  Project  Manager  - The Project  Manager  has more than 19 years of professional
  services  experience  in the water  resources  industry.

*  Successful  Track  Record  -  SA  has  provided  services  in water, transportation,  and
  government  markets  across California  for over 65 years, including  work for the City.
*  Project  Familiarity  -  SA  is familiar  with  the City  water's  water  system  as they  have
  provided  services  on prior  projects,  further,  they are the City's  current  on-call  consultants.
*  Experience  on Similar  Projects  - SA has completed  projects  with  similar  scope,  such as
  installation  of pipelines  on bridges  that cross freeways  and channels,  using  similar  methods
  and procedures

 PURPOSE  & BACKGROUND

The  City of South Gate (City) operates a municipal water system with approximately  135 miles
of water mains, serving over 14,250 customer accounts across residential, commercial,  and
industrial sectors. The existing 12-inch water main is aging and requires replacement to ensure
continued reliability and service. The pipeline crosses underneath the Firestone Blvd Bridge,
spanning  the 1-710 Freeway and the Los Angeles River. Due to the bridge location, the project
will necessitate  compliance with federal and state regulations, as well as close coordination with
local regulatory agencies.

The City is seeking a qualified Consultant that can successfully  provide Engineering  Design
Services to prepare Plans, Specifications  and Estimates for the Firestone Bridge Pipeline
Replacement  Project, City Project No. 737-WTR.  Services to be provided include project
management,  preliminary  engineering,  surveying,  design,  preparation  of final  plans,
specifications & estimates, and construction  support services, in accordance with Local, and
State requirements.  All services  are to be in conformance  with the Caltrans  design
requirements.

The scope of work involves replacing a corroded 1 2-inch water main that is suspended beneath
the Firestone Blvd Bridge. The replacement  pipeline will span approximately  3,200 linear feet.
Coordination  with Caltrans is required, as partial or full closures of the 1-710 Freeway may be
necessary during construction. Additionally, coordination with the u.s. Army Corps of Engineers,
California Department of Transportation  (Caltrans) and the Los Angeles Flood Control District
(LAFCD) will be required, as a portion of the work occurs over the Los Angeles River. Traffic
control measures will be implemented  on the Firestone Blvd Bridge, affecting on-ramps and off-
ramps to the freeway. Ifinstallation beneath the bridge is deemed infeasible, alternative methods
such as boring underneath the freeway may be considered.  Efforts will be made to minimize
disruptions to businesses and traffic, which may necessitate nighttime construction work.

The City is soliciting proposals from qualified Consultants that can successfully  provide
Engineering Design Services for this Project. The specific services noted are referenced under
the Introduction and Project Description heading above and are described in more detail in the
task below. The scope of work requested in this RFP is for the preparation of the full set of
construction documents necessary for construction and bidding. This includes the preparation
of the Plans, Specifications and Engineer's Estimates, obtaining all necessary permits and
clearances from other public agencies, construction support services and otherwork as specified
in this section. It shall be the Consultant's responsibility to ensure their proposal includes all

the project.

All design work shall adhere to the latest Caltrans' Standard Plans and Specifications, latest
edition of the Highway Design Manual, California MUTCD, American Waterworks Association,
and other applicable standards in effect as of the date of the Notice to Proceed. Design
services shall also adhere to City, State and County standards as applicable. All work shall
also conform to applicable federal, state, and local codes and other regulatory requirements,
The engineering and design services shall consider the following:

  Pipeline Design: Material selection (e.g., welded steel, HDPE, DIP), size, and

  bridges.
  Hydraulic Analysis: Capacity verification and surge protection considerations.

  Traffic Control Plan Development:  Required by Caltrans for work on/near the

  Permit Compliance  Plan: Ensure all permits are obtained and incorporated into

  Total  100

All proposals will be evaluated  by a South Gate Selection Committee  (Committee).  The
Committee may be composed of South Gate staff and other parties that may have expertise or
experience in the services described herein. The Committee will review the submittals and will
rank the proposals.  The evaluation of the proposals shall be within the sole judgement  and
discretion of the Committee. All contacts during the evaluation phase shall be through the South
Gate Project Manager only.

The selection committee may review the submitted proposals according to the above evaluation
criteria and weighting factors if necessary.  The committee will then establish a shortlist of
consultants who are considered to be best qualified to perform the contract work. The shortlist
will include enough qualified consultants to ensure that at least three consultants are shortlisted
for possible interviews, if deemed necessary.

If interviews are deemed necessary, the committee will reestablish a final ranking of the highest
ranked consultants  following  such interviews.  The Fee Proposal of the highest ranked
consultant will be opened and used to begin negotiations.  If agreement cannot be reached with
the highest ranked consultant,  then negotiations  will proceed with the next most qualified
consultant until a final consultant is selected.

The City staff will determine if an interview is necessary. If an interview is not necessary; the
project will be awarded to the highest rank proposal, subject to successful fee negotiations with
that Consultant.

 SECTION  Ill:  PROJECT  UNDERSTANDING,  APPROACH,  AND  SCOPE  OF WORK

 It is our understanding  that the City of South Gate (City) is seeking to engage a professional
 engineering  consultant  to provide engineering  design services for the Firestone Bridge Pipeline
 Replacement  Project, City Project No. 737-WTR  (Project). The Project involves the replacement
 of approximately  2,530 linear feet (LF) of existing 12-inch steel and cast iron pipe (CIP) water main
with new water main in Firestone  Boulevard,  from Rayo Avenue to National Avene, in order to
 improve the existing water system and address the corrosion issue of the aging pipeline beneath
the Firestone  Boulevard  bridges over the Los Angeles River and the 1-710 Freeway. The work
also involves reconnections  of existing water service laterals and a fire hydrant and tie-ins to
existing water mains. Furthermore,  the work includes replacement  of blow-offs, air release valves,
and water valves wherever applicable, trench pavement restoration,  and abandonment  of existing
mains all in compliance  with City Standards,  California MUTCD, the latest AW\/VA Standards,  and
the Project Specifications.  All design work within the alignment crossing the 1-710 Freeway are to
be in conformance  with the Caltrans design requirements.  The project will involve coordination
and permitting with LI.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Los Angeles Regional Water Quality
Control Board (RWQCB),  Caltrans, Los Angeles County Flood Control District (LACFCD),  Los
Angeles County Public Works Department  (LACDP\/S/), and others. In addition, work will also
include hydraulic evaluation,  structural analysis, and determination  of the recommended  method
for crossing the 1-710 Freeway and Los Angeles River.

FIGURE 1: PROJECT  LOCATION

The limits of Firestone  Boulevard  where  improvements  are to be implemented  are in an industrial
area with some segments  near commercial  properties, that would require specific construction
working hours (nighttime work) in order to minimize disruptions.  Moreover, the street consists of
concrete pavement  and AC pavement,  for which pavement would be rehabilitated  accordingly.

It is expected that the proposed water main will potentially require permits from and coordination
with the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) Division of Drinking Water (DD\/V) if
standard separations between water, sewer, and storm drain cannot be met.

The SA Associates engineering team is committed to maximizing all of its resources to provide the

also recently completed PS&E for Phase 2 with an approximate length of 17,000 LF. We also recently
completed final PS&E for two water main replacement projects for Long Beach utilities Department
(Queensway Drive and Ximeno Avenue) totaling 2,845 LF of 8-inch and 12-inch DIP. For the Ximeno
Avenue Project, we obtained the necessary permit with Caltrans. We also completed final PS&E for

Our team is very familiar with the permitting process and requirements for several agencies

The crucial part of this project is identifying the appropriate installation method for the proposed water

*  Channel  and Freeway  Crossinqs

  The proposed pipeline will cross the Los Angeles River channel, which is about 470 feet wide, and
  the 1-7'lO Freeway, which is approximately  225 feetwide. The channel and Freeway crossings will
  require encroachment  permits from LACFCD and Caltrans. The crossings may be constructed by
  tunneling under the channel and freeway (jack-and-bore),  hanging along the sides of the bridges,
  removing the existing pipelines and utilizing the same utility cells on the undersides the bridges.

  The utility cell may be a less expensive alternative.  During our preliminary research, we were
  unable to locate any as-builts from Los Angeles County or Caltrans forthe two bridges. We have
  noted from our site investigation that the bridge crossing over the Los Angeles River appears to
  have two existing utility openings available beneath each end of the bridge on the south side
  (added during the widening of the south side of the bridge); however, the openings may not be
  large enough to allow clearance for the proposed pipeline to pass through. If removing the
  existing 12-inch pipelines and utilizing the same existing utility openings is the desired option,
  the opening may not be wide enough accommodate  the size of a proposed pipeline casing, in
  which case, there will be no need fora casing. Another option is to tunnel underneath the channel
  using jack-and-bore  methods. If there is a large amount of data available for the Los Angeles
  River channel and 1-710 Freeway, we will be able to accurateiy depict the depth and area of the
  launching and receiving pits as well as accurately depict geotechnical  conditions at the site. The
  agencies having jurisdiction will have significant input on the depth of the bore, annular fill, pit
  distance from the channel and freeway rights-of-way,  and other items. We have prepared
  tunneling work of this scope before and will provide a design with the level of detail required by
  all parties to accomplish a successful project. The final option is hanging the pipe along one side
  of each bridge. This would require a fully welded steel pipe and will require permitting/approval.

TASK 3 - FIELD SURVEY

  Conduct a topographic survey to obtain necessary design topography for open trench water
  main replacement. All surface features within the right of way shall be located by the survey,
  including all utilities, valve covers, water meters, manholes, vaults, pull boxes, hydrants,
  catch basins, etc., as well as, depicting rights-of-way, edge of pavement, sidewalk,
  landscape, curb, gutter, cross gutters, any easement, utilities, monuments, stripe, and other
  items pertinent to a well-defined survey. The survey will also include elevations for flow line
  of existing sewers and storm drains in the project limits. The survey shall also provide
  baselines, bench marks, and all other basic survey control information. The basis of the
  vertical control shall be the most recent City benchmark elevations. All field topography shall
  be collected electronically using modern survey equipment for data processing and
  preparation of a digital AutoCAD file. It is important to note that all aspects of the two existing
  bridges will be captured in the survey (i.e., bridge deck, soffit, concrete, ties, surrounding
  fence, railings, gates, etc.) to ensure the accuracy of the overcrossing portion of the design.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH o.c. VACUUM,  INC. TO PROVIDE  SPECIALIZED
OPERATION  AND  MAINTENANCE  SERVICES  FOR  THE  STORM  WATER
DIVRESION  SYSTEM LOCATED  AT THE TJRBAN ORCHARD  PARK

PURPOSE:  The Urban Orchard Park construction improvements included a stormwater atid
wetland system that cleans runoff from the Bandini Channel and/or irrigates the park. Regular
specialty maintenance is needed to ensure proper operation and regulatory compliance. Staff
recommend awarding a three-year agreement, not to exceed $450,000, to QC Vacuum, Inc. (QC
Vac) to provide these specialized maintenance services.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will  consider:
  a.  Approving an Agreement with o.c. Vacuum, Inc. to provide operations and maintenance
  services for the storm water diversion system located at the Urban Orchard Park, for a
  three-year term, for an amount not to exceed $450,000, or $150,000 per year;
  b.  Authorizing  the City Manager to approve and execute amendments for a cumulative
  amount of $100,000;
  c.  Authorize the transfer of $190,000 in Measure W Funds from the Fiscal Year 2025/26
  Capital Improvement Program, Urban Orchard Project budget to the Fiscal Year 2025/26
  Operating Public Works Budget to fund first year services and contingency funds; and
  d.  Authorizing the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable to the City Attorney.

FISCALIMPACT:  ThereisnofiscalimpacttotheGeneralFund.TheproposedAgreementwill
be fully funded with $450,000 in Measure W Funds over a three-year term, at a rate of $150,000
annually. Funding for the first year is currently budgeted in the FY 2025/26 Capital Improvement
Program, of which $190,000 is proposed to be transfened to the Public Works Operating Budget
to support first-year services. The total project budget is $550,000, as summarized below.

  Budget  Year  I Services  Year 2 Services  Year 3 Services  Total
 Agreement  $150,000  $150,000  $150,000  $450,000
 Contingency  $40,000  $30,000  $30,000  $100,000
  Total  $550,000

ANALYSIS:  Construction  of the Urban Orchard Project was recently completed and included

  1  201
 installation  of a stormwater diversion system. The diversion system serves both NPDES
stormwater compliance and aesthetic purposes, as it integrates with and enhances the surrounding
wetlands. To ensure the system continues to function properly, specialized operations and
maintenance services are required at Urban Orchard Park, for which the subject agreement  is
recommended. The scope of services includes debris removal, vacuum cleaning, inspection, and
hydro-jetting of the Bandini Channel, stormwater inlets, vaults, reservoir, and pump stations, as
well as graffiti abatement along the Bandini Channel and maintenance of the wetland area.
Approval of this agreement will ensure ongoing compliance with stormwater regulations and
preserve the visual quality of the site.

The City issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) to find a contractor to handle ongoing maintenance
at Urban Orchard Park. One proposal was received from QC Vac, a company  with proven
experience maintaining  stormwater systems and treatment facilities.  After reviewing  their
proposal, staff determined that OC Vac is well qualified for the job and recommend awarding them
a contract for an amount not to exceed $450,000 for a three-year term, or $150,000 annually.

BACKGROUND:  The Urban Orchard Park officially opened to the public on July 12, 2025
and has a need for specialty services. The park includes a stormwater system and wetland area
designed to clean runoff from the Bandini Channel by capturing and treating both dry-weather and
some wet-weather flows. To keep the system working properly and continue improving  water
quality, regular maintenance is required. Under an agreement with the Los Angeles County Flood
Control District, the City is responsible for maintaining parts of the Bandini Charu'iel as well as
the stormwater inlets, vaults, reservoirs, and pump stations within Urban Orchard Park.

Staff recommend awarding the agreement to OC Vac, the sole proposer responding to the City's
Request for Proposals (RFP) for Urban Orchard Park Operations and Maintenance Services. The
RFP was issued on September 11, 2025, through PlanetBids, with proposals due by October 9,
2025. A selection committee composed of the Senior Engineer, Associate Engineer, and Assistant
Engineer reviewed QC Vac's proposal. The committee evaluated qualifications,  experience,
response times, and proposed fees, and determined that QC Vac is well qualified to perform the
required services. OC Vac offers the following strengths:

  *  Experienced  Project  Manager:  Over 20 years of professional  experience  in the water
  resources industry.

  *  Proven  Performance:  More  than  45 years  of experience  providing  environmental  and
  maintenance  services  across  California,  including  previous  work  for the City.

  *  Project Familiarity:  Recently provided emergency maintenance services  at Urban
  Orchard Park, demonstrating la'iowledge of the site's stormwater system.

  *  Relevant Experience:  Successfully completed similar  projects  involving  stormwater
  treatment and maintenance for other public agencies.

 INTRODUCTION  AND  PROJECT  DESCRIPTION

The City of South Gate (City) is seeking a qualified Contractor  to provide maintenance  services
for the Urban Orchard  Park Operation  & Maintenance  Project. The urban Orchard  Park was
developed  to improve water quality within the LACFCD DDI 23 (Bandini Channel),  which serves
the City of South Gate and ultimately the Los Angeles River Watershed,  by capturing  and treating
dry-weather  flows and a portion of wet-weather runoff.

Flows from the Bandini Channel  are diverted into a pretreatment  device through a drop inlet.
Following  pretreatment,  the water is pumped  into an underground  storage  reservoir and
conveyed to the open-air wetland. The treated water is then reused for irrigation within the park.
To ensure the long-term  performance  of the system, continued  pollutant removal,  and overall
project sustainability,  the City requires a comprehensive  maintenance  program.

SCOPE  OF SERVICES

The City is soliciting proposals from qualified Contractor  that can successfully  provide maintenance
services for Urban Orchard Park. The specific services are described  in detail in the task below.
This includes maintenance  of a storm drain diversion  system, pretreatment  system, pump station,
active controls, onsite irrigation system, decomposed  granite path at LACFCD maintenance  access
road.

The specific  tasks for this scope  of work are as specified  as follows:

  SUBJECT-  ATTORNEY  FEE AGREEMENTS  WITH  OUTSIDE  COUNSEL

  PURPOSE:  To  approve  attorney  retainer  agreements  with  the  law  firms  of  Liebert  Cassidy
  Whitmore;  Aleshire  & Wynder;  Lewis  Brisbois;  Rothans,  Carpenter  & Dumont;  and Frost BrownTodd
  to provide  legal services  to the City.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Attorney  Retainer  Agreement  with  the law firni  of (1) Liebert  Cassidy  Whitmore;
  (2) Aleshire  & Wynder;  (3) Lewis  Brisbois:  (4) Rothans,  Carpenter  & Dumont;  and Frost
  Brown  Todd  LLP  to continue  to provide  legal  services  to the City  related  to consulting,
  representational  and legal services  and
  b.  Authorize  the City  Manager  to execute  such agreements  in a forin  acceptable  to the City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  Estimated  impact  is dependent  on usage, The exact amount  of fees to be billed
  by the law firm  is not known  at this time,  as it depends  on the services  rendered  on an as-needed  basis.
  Rates offered  by each firm  are dependent  on the frequency  of use.  Some rates are contemplated  to be
  attributed  to special  funds  that would  not impact  the City's  general  fund.

  ANALYSIS:  The referenced  firms  are requesting  approval  of fee rate adjustments  to their  standard
  retainer  agreements,  as follows:  Aleshire  requests  rates ranging  from  $258 for Associates  and $297
  for Partners  and lower  rates for law clerks,  paralegals  and document  clerks.  The firin  correctly  notes
  that its rates  are below  market  rates.  Liebert  Cassidy  seeks rates of $475  senior  partners,  Senior
  Counsel  at $390,  and associates  at between  $295-$370.  The firm  seeks other lower  rates for staff as
  noted  in its agreement.  Lewis  Brisbois  seeks rates of $325 for partners,  and $275 for associates,  and
  lower  rates for other  staff.  Carpenter  Rothans  seeks rates of $325 for partners,  and $275 associates.
  Depending  on each specific  firm,  these rates would  become  effective  as of July 1, 2025, and be subject
  to adjustment  as of July 1, 2025.

  Frost  Brown  Todd  requests  a flat  retainer  of $22,500  per month  for work  perfonned  by the City
  Attorney,  including  time spent attending  City Council  meetings,  attending  meetings,  reviewing  agenda
  bills  and overseeing  the work  processed  by the City  Attorney.  This is in line with  prior  expenditures
  for similar  scopes of work  and is intended  to assist the City  with  financial  planning.  The firm  seeks

  311
 rates of $360 for partners,  $340 for associates,  and $200 for paralegals  for litigation  and transaction
work.  These rates would  not become  effective  until  January  1, 2026.

The firm  would  anticipate  seeking  a 4% increase  on January  1, 2027,  and 2028.  The deferral  of
any increase  until  January  1 is intended  to delay  increases  in rates that would  have occurred  July

 2022.

 (a) Each person appointed  by a board of supervisors  to be a member  of a board of

that is within  the district.
(b) Each person  appointed  by a city council  to be a member  of a board of trustees
shall be a voter in that city and a resident  of that portion  of the city that is within
the district.
(c) Notwithstanding  any other provision  of law including  the common  law doctrine
that precludes  the simultaneous  holding  of incompatible  offices,  a member  of a city
council  may be appointed  and may serve as a member  of a board of trustees  if that
person also meets the other applicable  qualifications  of this chapter.
(d) It is the intent  of the Legislature  that persons  appointed  to boards of trustees
have experience,  training,  and education  in fields that will assist in the governance
of the districts.
(e) All trustees  shall exercise  their independent  judgment  on behalf of the interests
of the residents,  property  owners,  and the public as a whole in furthering  the
purposes  and intent  of this chapter.  The trustees  shall represent  the interests  of the
public as a whole and not solely the interests  of the board of supervisors  or the city
council that appointed  them.

  added on the city's  website  food  bank resources.

  Luis  Frausto,  Director  of Administrative  Services,  stated that the recent
  legislation  related  to the requirement  to provide  broadcast  or call-in

  features  to the City  Council  Meetings  is being  researched  by city staff.
  Vendors were brought in to look at options the city has. One of the options
  being looked at is going to allow for a call-in feature. This is an unfunded
  mandate.

  Jon Hamilton,  Director  of Human  Resources,  wished  everyone  a happy
  Veterans  Day.

  Manny  Arana,  Chief  of Police,  reminded  everyone  that on Saturday,
  November  15, 2025,  from  10:00  a.m. to 3:00 p.m.,  is the Family  Day at
  the Park at South  Gate Park.

  Rob Houston,  City  Manager,  clarified  why the Finance  Director  is talking

  about IT. Mr. Fausto  oversights  is both Finance  and IT.

  Raul F. Salinas,  City Attorney,  had nothing  to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer,  stated that outside  the Legacy  Complex

  the schools  are creating  a public  safety issue on Legacy  Lane and Tweedy.
  He has provided  the information  to City  Manager  and Chief  of Police.

  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk,  stated that Rotary  will  be serving  Thanksgiving

  dinner  to needy  families  in the community.  She may be reached  for tickets.

  Council  Member  Avalos  expressed  appreciation  and gratitude  to veterans

  for their  service,  noting  that military  service  can have a lasting  impact  on

  individuals.  She emphasized  the importance  of showing  returning  service

  members  patience,  kindness  and understanding.  While  recognizing  that

  although  veterans  may return  changed,  they remain  the same individuals
  deserving  of respect,  particularly  in light  of the freedoms  their  service
  helps protect.

  Council  MemberAvalos  also reported  attending  the State of the City
  event,  describing  it as informative  and expressing  appreciation  for the

  presentations  by city leadership  and the mayor.  Additionally,  she noted
  that the Southeast  Water  Coalition  meeting  was scheduled  but

  subsequently  canceled  and aru"iounced  that a Vector  Control  meeting  is

  scheduled  to take place on Thursday.

  donated.  Two police  cruisers  were filled  up.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  stated that over hundred  players  participated  in a mini
  tournament.  He donated  championship  rings to the kids that participated.
  He mentioned  that each player,  parents  and businesses  donated  toys. A

  shows up with  a car full  of toys and Vice Mayor  Barron's  father,  who
  spends $1,000  dollars  on toys.

  21s', the SELA  Kiwanis  is hosting  their  second  annual  Taste of SELA
  banquet  and asked to visit  their  Instagram  page at selakiwanis.org  to
